html:
The Mukti Bahini, meaning "liberation army", was the Bengali force that fought the Pakistan Army in the Bangladesh Liberation War of 1971.

It grew out of the mutiny of Bengali units, the East Bengal Regiment and the East Pakistan Rifles, along with police and many students and villagers, after Operation Searchlight. Colonel M. A. G. Osmani was its commander in chief. The government in exile, formed in April at a border village in the East, gave it political direction in the name of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, who was in prison in West Pakistan.

India gave it camps, weapons and training. The regular units fought across the border, and the guerrillas sabotaged ports, bridges and roads, and ambushed the army. In the monsoon the Bengalis kept up the pressure.

When India entered the war in December in the Indo-Pakistani War, the Mukti Bahini worked with the Indian army in a joint command and helped it advance fast on Dhaka. Pakistan's forces surrendered on 16 December.
sum: The Mukti Bahini, meaning "liberation army", was the Bengali force that fought the Pakistan Army in the Bangladesh Liberation War of 1971.
